# The rank of 3×3 matrix multiplication over F2 is 23

Programs, data and the Lean 4 formalization for the paper *The rank of 3×3 matrix multiplication over F2 is 23* by
Tejasvi S. Tomar ([doi:10.5281/zenodo.23236158](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23236158)). Archived at [doi:10.5281/zenodo.23236154](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23236154).

## Statement

Every decomposition of the 3×3 matrix multiplication tensor over F2 has at least 23 terms (`Top.RankGe23`; the final theorem is `R22B.rank_ge_23`). With
Laderman's algorithm this gives rank 23 (`R22B.rank_eq_23`). `R22B.recursive_23` gives Rudich and Rousseau's statement about recursive algorithms with 23 in place of 22.

## What is proved, what is evaluated, what is trusted

See Section 8 of the paper. In short:
- `lean/` holds the checkers, their soundness proofs and the reductions of the paper. All of these use only the axioms
  `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- The certificates are checked by evaluating the checkers with `native_decide`, which adds one axiom per batch and trusts
  the Lean compiler and runtime. The certificates are regenerated and checked in a stream, and they are not stored.
- The generators in `cpp/` and the queue in `scripts/` are not trusted: a wrong item makes a check or a covering proof fail.

The run: 20.95 h wall time, 4381024 batches, manifest sha256 a9abb910584e8d00b26c97841764e039fa93949d86851b29057a50442243382f, checker library MANIFEST.sha256 fba403eca962431b967f90fa44d299e61779cb91d29ba5ade853c86c017a88af.
Each batch recorded the hashes of the compiled checker library and modules it loaded, and only batches built against the final library were combined. Of 744 batches selected by a hash of their names, 382 were evaluated again with Lean's interpreter, without the library, before the final theorem was assembled, with no difference (data/run/run_summary.json lists them by kind).

## Layout

| path | content |
|---|---|
| `paper/` | the paper (LaTeX source and PDF) |
| `lean/` | the Lean development in module form (Lean v4.30.0, Mathlib v4.30.0); the final file is `lean/R22B/FinalTop.lean`, and `lean/PROVENANCE.md` says how the tree relates to the frozen build and which generated modules it imports |
| `lean/tools/` | build and validation tools of the module port |
| `data/lean/` | `INDEX.tsv`: the files that the Lean loaders read at elaboration time (path, bytes, sha256). The files are in the Zenodo record (`EXTERNAL.md`); `scripts/fetch_data.sh` downloads, unpacks and checks them |
| `data/tables/` | the capacity tables, kept rows and static tables read by the generators (`.zst`: decompress with `zstd -d`) |
| `data/RECIPE.txt` | the exact options of the certificate generators |
| `data/checks/` | the checks of Table 4 of the paper: `controls/` (positive controls of the completion search) and `split_flattening/` (the excess system on the six known 23-term decompositions in `decompositions23.txt`), each with its run script and outputs |
| `data/classes/routes.tsv` | for each raised class (numbered as in Rudich and Rousseau's Lean table): new bound, route (enumeration checked by the kernel or natively, or monotonicity transport) and dependencies |
| `data/run/` | the certified run: summary, where each number came from, per-item manifest, list of native axioms |
| `cpp/` | the certificate generators (`search/`, `enum/`), the completion search (`tsolve/`) and shared headers |
| `scripts/queue/` | the job queue used to distribute the run |
| `scripts/native/` | the native run: checker library build (`mklib.sh`), per-batch checker (`nchk_batch.sh`), glue generator, end check |

## Building

- `scripts/fetch_data.sh` downloads `data/lean` from the Zenodo record and checks every file against `data/lean/INDEX.tsv`.
- `cpp/build.sh` builds the generators and the completion search (g++, OpenSSL, HiGHS).
- The Lean development builds with Lean v4.30.0 and Mathlib v4.30.0: `lean/tools/pbuild.py` compiles the modules in import
  order. `scripts/native/mklib.sh` builds the shared library of compiled checkers that the batches load.
- `data/RECIPE.txt` gives the exact generator options for each case of the search.

The proof imports the Lean proof of R ≥ 22 by Rudich and Rousseau, which is not copied here. Fetch it from
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23047901 (archive `lb22_zenodo.zip`, 82,480,696 bytes, md5 c72def5ec5a272b3a60f6a43b2f99066)
and put its sources on the Lean path (see `lean/tools/pbuild.py`).
